question.text: The investment manager's remuneration typically includes:

answer.text: Management fees from the fund and additional returns based on fund performance and the investment-agreement terms
A percentage of the stock exchange's trading volume

explanation.text: The Logic: The management company is generally remunerated through management fees (up to 2.5% of committed capital during the commitment period) and additional returns tied to fund performance under the terms of the investment agreement. Individual fund managers, in turn, are typically paid by the management company through salary and/or profit sharing. The Trap: Management fees are paid regardless of performance, while the additional / performance-based component is contingent on fund performance and the contractual terms — the two are not the same and should not be conflated. Note: Replaced the unsourced "1.5-2.5%" range with the workbook-supported ceiling of up to 2.5% of committed capital during the commitment period, and removed the unsourced investor-friendly fee-structure advice. Keyed answer is unchanged.
